summary: Compact request rows, produce host metadata deltas and execute bounded independent CPU batches with completion notification
implementation_scope: Ready-row compaction, immutable stable-slot metadata snapshots and bounded incremental patches, owned candidate copies, single-use commit handoff and retirement barrier; native uploads and model batching are external; C++20 HostBatch executes independent CPU tasks through Core async batch lifecycle

agent_guidance.use_when: Several requests produce variable candidate rows with independent readiness and lifetime
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Only one request runs, or existing core/engine staging already supplies the same handoff
provides: Ordered ready-row selection with admitted row limit
Copied and reserved candidate groups consumed once at commit
Stable request/generation slots with immutable retained snapshots and changed-row byte patches
Exact-base delta validation, atomic host apply and independently ordered row gathers
Real asynchronous host batch execution with private result storage and retained owners
engine_supplies: Active request/generation mapping and model execution
Success checks beyond done(), byte reservations and partial-failure cleanup
Snapshot and native replica memory reservations, ordered patch uploads and physical reader retention
Thread-safe shared model inspection and independent per-operation workspaces, accounting and cancellation
preserve: Compact rows retain original request/generation identity
Copy and reserve before borrowed storage is invalidated
Commit success before publication; physical completion before retirement
adapt: Compaction layout, group size and request selection policy
Reservation representation and native dependency handling
Physical row selectors for optional pooled graphs, independent of logical request/generation identity

code_files.purpose: Ready-row compaction, owned candidate copies, single-use commit handoff and retirement barrier; model batching is external
Stable keyed metadata rows, immutable snapshots, changed-byte deltas and atomic host replica/gather updates
Owned CPU batch execution, nonblocking future readiness, single-use commit and joining lifetime for Core pipeline

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ and standard library for the host reference; backend hardware is an engine choice; C++20 host threads for native helper
requires.model: Engine with independent request state and variable nonempty candidate rows
requires.workload: Concurrent requests with declared per-request output budgets and physical receipts

contract.input: Row identities, candidates, physical readiness, per-request output budgets and reservation hooks
contract.output: Copied StagedGroup rows and a pollable RetirementBarrier
contract.ownership: Consumer owns state/group commit. Native core owns admission, scheduling, publication, poison/quarantine and final producer/backend retirement.
contract.failure: Reject duplicate/unsettled rows, excess candidates and repeat commit; a failed model callback is not automatically rolled back
contract.core_boundary: Map compact rows to native Model concurrent callbacks; preserve the header contract rather than copying a worker/runtime.

dependencies: C++20 standard library and Core SDK for HostBatch

validation.host: Host fixtures and worked example cover row compaction, copies, budgets, failed commit and independent retirement; 500 metadata mutation/gather comparisons, stale deltas, slot rebinding, immutable old readers and invalid-patch non-publication
validation.native: C++ CPU integration tests exercise independent overlap, ordered output, cancellation, refill, prepare/submit/producer/commit failure, stale membership, deadline cleanup and quarantine; immediate/racing completion notification, no idle batch polling, retained trace spans and slow/failure classification; device arithmetic remains unqualified
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim
